title: Add a Google button to DuckDuckGo
question: How do I repeat a DuckDuckGo search on Google in one click?
answer: Without an extension, add !g to your search: DuckDuckGo's bang sends the query straight to Google. To get a button instead, the usermods script on this page adds a Google tab to the DuckDuckGo tab bar, next to All, Images and Videos. It links to a Google search for the same words and follows along when you search again.
prompt: Add a Google button to DuckDuckGo results that runs the same search on Google.
details:
The script reads the search from the `q` parameter in the address bar and links to `https://www.google.com/search?q=...`. DuckDuckGo redraws its tab bar on each new search, so a MutationObserver puts the button back and updates its link. It copies the style of an existing tab.

It only adds a link: nothing is sent to Google until you click it.

alternatives.title: The !g bang
alternatives.body: Type `!g` anywhere in a DuckDuckGo search, for example `bread recipe !g`, and DuckDuckGo forwards it to Google. Other bangs work the same way: `!b` for Bing, `!w` for Wikipedia.

check.expect: (() => { const links = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="duckbar"] nav a')].filter((a) => a.href === 'https://www.google.com/search?q=how%20to%20bake%20bread'); return links.length === 1 && links[0].checkVisibility() && links[0].textContent.trim() === 'Google'; })()
check.intact: (() => { const results = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="result"]')].filter((r) => r.checkVisibility()); const all = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="duckbar"] nav a')].find((a) => a.textContent.trim() === 'All'); return results.length >= 5 && !!all && all.checkVisibility(); })()
